data.gender_notes: Gratian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gratian is derived from the Latin word 'gratia', which means 'pleasing' or 'gracious'. It was a common name for those who were favored by the gods in ancient Rome. In Christianity, Gratian is the name of several saints, including Saint Gratian of Cologne, who is the patron saint of travelers, and Saint Gratian of Prague, who is remembered for his acts of charity and generosity.

data.etymology: Gratian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Favored, pleasing, gracious.”

in_greek.name: Γρατιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Γρατιανός είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από το λατινικό 'Gratianus', που σημαίνει 'εύνοια' ή 'καλοσύνη'. Το όνομα αυτό δεν αναφέρεται ρητά στη Νέα Διαθήκη, αλλά έχει ιστορική σημασία στην πρώιμη Εκκλησία και συνδέεται με την παράδοση της Χριστιανικής πίστης.

in_latin.name: Gratian

In early Christian tradition, the name Gratian was used to denote someone who was gracious or beloved. Historically, Gratian was also the name of a 4th-century Roman Emperor and a Christian martyr.
